chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn, from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The sun eclipsed while I was in the bathhouse, and I learned of it after I had exited, so I did not make up the prayer.
ai.seo_question: Is the eclipse prayer (Salat al-Kusuf) required to be made up if missed?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that the sun eclipsed while he was in the bathhouse; he realized it only after exiting and consequently did not perform the eclipse prayer as a make-up (Qada). This incident establishes the scholarly consensus in Shia jurisprudence that Salat al-Kusuf is a Sunnah Mu'akkadah rather than a strict obligation, meaning it is not required to be made up if missed due to valid reasons like bathing or sleep. The narration highlights the flexibility in performing this prayer, emphasizing its role as a sign of God's power rather than a rigid ritual duty.
